summary: Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1840) and served as Bibliothekar at the Russian Academy of Sciences from around 1852 to 1879.
Anton Westermann was a German scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1823–1828) and spent his career there as a faculty member from around 1834 to 1869.

Antonino Forte specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hōbōgirin (~1976–1986), Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale (~1982–1999), and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006), alongside affiliations with EFEO and ISEAS.
Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He completed his studies at Fordham University (~1965–1968) and held a post at Stony Brook University from circa 1968 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend ter Haar in 2010, and served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was an Indian scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya and earned a PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he taught Pali, later directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Archibald Edward Gough was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Monier Monier-Williams (~1863–1866). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Presidency University, Kolkata (~1878–1895, 1914), and served as Principal of Aliah University (~1881–1895, 1914).

Arindam Chakrabarti is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2009–2014).
Arinde L. Jonker is an Indologist who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018). Her studies were supervised by Peter Bisschop alongside instruction from Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arlo Griffiths is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at Harvard and Leiden University (PhD ~2004 under Henk Bodewitz), he held posts at Groningen (~2003–2005), Leiden (attested 2002–2008), and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2008).

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a German historian and archaeologist. He studied at the Athenaeum (~1776–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1784), where he subsequently served as a professor from circa 1787 to 1842.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served as Deputy Professor and then Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1899), as well as a Fellow of Balliol College (~1899–1926).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was a Scottish Indologist and linguist who studied at Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under A. A. Macdonell. He worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) before serving as Regius Professor at Edinburgh (~1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen was a Danish scholar of Iranian philology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from circa 1893 to 1903 and was appointed professor extraordinarius of Iranian philology there in 1919.
Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Bedford School and King's College London (~1857–1860), he worked as an officer in the Indian Civil Service between circa 1860 and 1880.

Arthur F. Wright was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford (~1931–1935), Oxford (~1935–1937), and Harvard (~1935–1947), and served as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale University (~1959–1976).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian. After studying at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett, he held professorships at the University of London, SOAS (~1958–1965), Australian National University (~1965–1978), and the Asiatic Society (~1985–1986).

Arthur McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He pursued doctoral studies in Sanskrit and Indian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Diana L. Eck, Parimal G. Patil, and Palri Sangye.
